messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: service=redwood-edge TLS handshake error rate >7% across prod-us-east-1 over 5m
pagerduty: Paging on-call: @sara.nguyen
sara.nguyen: I'm active. pulling ingress logs and checking synthetic monitors. any direct customer tickets? @customer-success
customer-success: 3 customers flagged, mostly mobile SDKs and web users behind specific ISPs. one high-priority ticket from MobileX.
carla.net: joining to check LB termination and cert distribution. will look at k8s secrets and ingress pods.
vikram.s: grabbing tcpdump from edge-az1 and az2 nodes. attaching small snippets below.

T+00:05 vikram.s: tcpdump fragment capture from edge-az1 (10.2.4.11):

09:47:21.987654 IP 203.0.113.45.53012 > 10.2.4.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 231:489, ack 1, win 229, length 258
09:47:21.987662 IP (frag 1) 203.0.113.45 > 10.2.4.11: ip-proto-6, frag offset 0
09:47:21.987670 IP (frag 2) 203.0.113.45 > 10.2.4.11: ip-proto-6, frag offset 1480

vikram.s: looks like handshake bytes are split into fragments on some flows.

T+00:10 carla.net: cert-sync logs show last secret sync to kube-ingress controller failed on node edge-az2 at 03:20 UTC with transient i/o timeout, then retried. most nodes show new cert, but edge-az2 had a retry and old cert lingered for ~10 minutes. grabbing exact logs.

cert-sync snippet:
I0506 03:20:02 sync secret redwood-edge-cert to node edge-az2: starting
E0506 03:20:05 error: write timeout to etcd endpoint
I0506 03:20:35 retry sync succeded

carla.net: this could cause a mismatch if traffic routed to that node while some clients had stricter TLS stacks. need to confirm.

T+00:18 sara.nguyen: synthetic monitor output shows spike in tls.alert_40 across multiple vantage points; mobile probes on cellular networks worst impacted. also seeing increased TCP RSTs during initial handshake window.

T+00:25 leo.t: ran tracepath from an external probe to edge IP 203.0.113.45, got a PMTU reduction at a transit hop to 1420

tracepath snippet:
1?: pmtu 1500
 1: 10.1.0.1                 0.201ms
 2: 172.31.0.1               0.453ms
 3: 198.51.201.1             1.234ms pmtu 1420
 4: 203.0.113.45            12.345ms reached

leo.t: PMTU 1420 would force fragmentation for ClientHello with SNI+ALPN+extensions.

T+00:32 vikram.s: VPC flow logs for affected subnets show flows with SYN from client, then multiple retransmissions and eventually RSTs from our nodes. attaching sample lines.

T+00:40 hypothesis tracker (in-thread) by sara.nguyen:
- H1: cert mismatch on a subset of ingress pods due to failed secret sync -> evidence: cert-sync error on edge-az2; counter-evidence: many nodes report correct cert and openssl probes show correct chain after sync settled; still plausible for short window.
- H2: PMTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello to be dropped -> evidence: tracepath pmtu 1420; tcpdump shows IP fragments for TLS handshake; synthetic failures concentrated on networks that block ICMP fragmentation-needed; mitigation will test MSS clamp.
- H3: VPC peering MTU mismatch or jumbo frames set incorrectly in an intermediate peer causing reassembly issues -> evidence: cloud peer config shows nonstandard MTU on one peering link; opening cloud ticket.

T+00:52 quick mitigation options discussed:
- Apply TCP MSS clamp on ingress host level (iptables mangle rule) to enforce max MSS 1360; low-customer-notice change.
- Temporarily divert traffic away from edge-az2 (which had cert-sync hiccup) via weighted routing; causes latency for some users.
- Force restart of ingress pods on edge-az2 to ensure certs are reloaded; risk: transient 502s.

T+01:00 sara.nguyen: executing MSS clamp on two canaries in az1 and az2:

# iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360

T+01:07 infra-bot: Canary metrics: canary-az1 tls.handshake_success improved from 78% -> 98%, canary-az2 improved from 74% -> 96% after MSS clamp.

customer-success: MobileX confirms partial recovery for their users; will keep watching.

T+01:20 carla.net: restarted ingress pods on edge-az2 to pick up certs after confirming sync success. post-restart openssl probe shows correct cert chain.

T+01:30 sara.nguyen: interim analysis: likely chain: PMTU drop + ICMP filtering caused fragmentation of ClientHello (H2 primary). cert-sync blip on edge-az2 was a secondary confusion factor but not the dominant failure mode. VPC peering MTU mismatch still being investigated as root upstream cause.

Status on hypotheses:
- H1: possible but limited window; status moved to investigated and not primary.
- H2: primary; evidence: fragments in tcpdump, PMTU report, immediate improvement after MSS clamp.
- H3: contributing factor; cloud provider ticket OPEN-8821 created to check peering MTU and underlying transit path.

T+01:42 mitigation plan and owners (in-thread):
- Short-term: keep MSS clamp active on edge hosts and monitor (owner: sara.nguyen).
- Short-to-mid-term: add ingress-level MSS clamp and l7 handling in ingress controller (owner: carla.net, PR open).
- Mid-term: cloud provider to fix peering MTU mismatch or update transit filtering config (owner: maria.ops, cloud ticket OPEN-8821).
- Post-incident: update cert-sync tool to detect and block marking rotation complete until all ingress nodes confirm reload (owner: carla.net).

T+02:00 handoff: @sara.nguyen handing incident to @leo.t for overnight watch and postmortem writeup.

sara.nguyen: handoff notes:
- Incident start: 2026-05-10T09:47 UTC (pagerduty triggered).
- Symptom: spike in TLS handshake failures (alert 40) and 502/523s, disproportionately affecting mobile/cellular clients and some ISP ranges.
- Immediate actions: MSS clamp applied to edges, ingress pods restarted on affected node, cloud provider ticket opened.
- Next steps: monitor canaries, merge ingress PR, confirm cloud provider resolution, publish postmortem and customer-facing note.

leo.t: taking over. I'll watch metrics for 8h, assemble timeline, and draft postmortem. ping me for any regressions.

customer-success: preparing customer-facing summary; asks for final ETA on permanent fix once cloud provider responds.

T+03:30 final in-thread summary before closing pager:
- Affected customers: MobileX, FinPaySub, AnalyticsCo (detailed list in OPEN-8821 ticket)
- Impact window: ~09:47-11:10 UTC, approx 0.8% of requests in region-us-east-1 affected
- Root cause: PMTU/fragmentation due to transit hop enforcing lower MTU (1420) combined with ICMP filtering that prevented proper PMTU discovery; cert sync transient on one node confused triage but was not main cause.
- Mitigation: MSS clamp on hosts, ingress change in flight, cloud provider engaged for peering MTU fix.
- Owners: maria.ops (cloud ticket), carla.net (ingress PR & cert-sync changes), sara.nguyen (mitigation and runbook updates), leo.t (postmortem + watch).

maria.ops: adding runbook item: if TLS alert 40 spike and tcpdump shows fragments, assume PMTU problem and apply MSS clamp; escalate to cloud provider.

leo.t: will publish postmortem draft to #postmortems and link back. closing active pager now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Pager closed by leo.t at 2026-05-10T12:51:16Z
